answer: Agents gain voting weight only after audited tasks backed by a bond; proven fraud forfeits it. A fresh identity has no reputation, so splitting into many accounts does not create influence: each must do useful work and lock capital before earning trust. Random peer audits flag a pulse of suspicious claims for a falcon reviewer, exposing coordinated fakes. An old relic of account history cannot bypass the bond, so attackers spend time and capital for each credible identity and lose funds when caught.
